winter-1924.summary: Held in Chamonix, France, as an International Winter Sports Week and later recognised as the first Winter Games.
facts: Curling was also contested, but its medals weren't officially recognized until 2006.
Norway and Finland took more than half the medals.

winter-1928.summary: Held in St. Moritz, Switzerland, where unusually warm weather forced the cancellation of the 10,000 m speed skating race.
facts: The skeleton sled event made its debut on the Cresta Run.
A warm foehn wind forced bobsled to be cut from four runs to two.

winter-1932.summary: Held in Lake Placid, United States, in the middle of the Great Depression, with only 17 nations taking part.
facts: The cost of crossing the Atlantic kept many athletes from Europe at home.
A medal podium was used at the Olympics for the first time, giving the ceremony its modern look.

winter-1936.summary: Staged by Nazi Germany in Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Bavaria, as a propaganda showcase.
facts: Alpine skiing became an official sport for the first time.
Sonja Henie won her third straight Olympic figure skating title.

winter-1948.summary: Resumed after a 12-year wartime break in St. Moritz, in neutral Switzerland, without Germany or Japan.
facts: South Korea competed for the first time, sending three speed skaters.
Norway and Sweden finished with identical medal counts, so no single nation could be ranked first.

winter-1952.summary: Held in Oslo, Norway, where the flame was lit from the hearth of ski pioneer Sondre Norheim's birthplace.
facts: Hjalmar Andersen of the host nation won three gold medals in speed skating.
Women's cross-country skiing was introduced for the first time.

winter-1956.summary: Held in Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy, where the Soviet Union topped the standings on its debut.
facts: They were the first to be televised to multiple countries.
A female athlete took the Olympic athletes' oath for the first time.

winter-1960.summary: Held in Squaw Valley, California, United States, where bobsleigh was left out because no track was built.
facts: Walt Disney staged the opening ceremony.
Biathlon joined the program as an official sport for the first time.

winter-1964.summary: Held in Innsbruck, Austria, where snow was so scarce that soldiers trucked it in from the Brenner Pass.
facts: For the first time, the Winter Games flame was lit at Olympia in Greece.
Luge debuted as an official sport with three events.

winter-1968.summary: Held in Grenoble, France, where home favourite Jean-Claude Killy swept all three alpine skiing events.
facts: Gender and doping tests were carried out for the first time.
Color television coverage began in earnest.

winter-1972.summary: The first Winter Games in Asia, held in Sapporo, Japan, where the hosts swept the normal hill ski jumping podium.
facts: Dutch speed skater Ard Schenk won three gold medals.
An alpine skier was expelled just before the opening for having accepted money.

winter-1976.summary: Taken over by Innsbruck, Austria, 12 years after it last hosted, when Denver pulled out after a public vote.
facts: Home hero Franz Klammer won the downhill in front of an Austrian crowd.
To mark its second time as host, both the 1964 cauldron and a new one were lit.

winter-1980.summary: Held in Lake Placid, United States, where a team of college hockey players beat the Soviet Union in the “Miracle on Ice.”
facts: Eric Heiden won all five speed skating events.
Artificial snow was laid down for Olympic competition for the first time.

winter-1984.summary: Held in Sarajevo, Yugoslavia, the first Winter Games staged in a socialist country.
facts: Eight years later, the city became a battleground in a civil war.
Torvill and Dean received perfect artistic-impression scores from every judge in ice dance.

winter-1988.summary: Held in Calgary, Canada, where a bobsleigh team from snowless, tropical Jamaica competed for the first time.
facts: The team's story became the 1993 film “Cool Runnings.”
Ski jumper Eddie Edwards became famous for finishing last.

winter-1992.summary: Held in Albertville, France, the last Winter Games staged in the same year as the Summer Games.
facts: Kim Ki-hoon won South Korea's first Winter Olympic gold medal, in short track.
A reunified Germany competed as a single team and finished first.

winter-1994.summary: Held in Lillehammer, Norway, just two years after the previous Games, to stagger the Winter and Summer Games.
facts: The attack on figure skater Nancy Kerrigan erupted just before the Games.
One ice hockey arena was built inside a cavern carved out of a mountain.

winter-1998.summary: Held in Nagano, Japan, where snowboarding became an official sport and NHL players took part for the first time.
facts: Women's ice hockey was also added to the programme for the first time.
The host nation won gold in the team ski jump.

winter-2002.summary: Held in Salt Lake City, United States, after a bid bribery scandal and five months after the 9/11 attacks.
facts: Kim Dong-sung's disqualification in short track sparked a major controversy.
After judging manipulation in figure skating came to light, gold medals were awarded to two pairs.

winter-2006.summary: Held in Turin, Italy, where South Korea won six of the eight short track gold medals.
facts: Jin Sun-yu and Ahn Hyun-soo each won three short track golds.
The torch traveled 11,300 kilometers across Italy over 64 days.

winter-2010.summary: Held in Vancouver, Canada, where the hosts won their first gold on home soil and topped the gold medal table.
facts: Kim Yuna won figure skating with a world-record score of 228.56.
The host nation won the ice hockey final in overtime.

winter-2014.summary: Held in Sochi, a subtropical Black Sea resort in Russia, and the most expensive Games ever staged.
facts: Systematic doping came to light, and several medals were stripped.
As medals were stripped and restored again and again, the top spot in the gold medal count changed hands several times.

winter-2018.summary: Held in Pyeongchang, South Korea, where the two Koreas marched together and fielded a unified women's ice hockey team.
facts: The white tiger Soohorang served as mascot.
The women's curling team won silver and became a national sensation.

winter-2022.summary: Held in Beijing, China, which became the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Games.
facts: Nearly all the snow at the venues was artificial.
Because of COVID-19, spectators were effectively barred.

winter-2026.summary: Co-hosted by Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy, where Klæbo swept six gold medals.
facts: Cortina d'Ampezzo hosted the Winter Games again after 70 years.
The venues were spread across three regions of northern Italy.
